findings.title: Invalid Ruby prevents the discussion template from rendering
findings.body: The template closes its conditional with `end if` rather than `end`. The trailing `if` has no condition, so ERB generates invalid Ruby and rendering raises a syntax error. Every embed request that finds an existing topic fails instead of displaying the discussion. Replace this with `end` and add a controller test that renders the actual view.

findings.title: Imported feed HTML is published without sanitization
findings.body: Feed contents are passed through `absolutize_urls`, which only parses and rewrites links, and then saved using `raw_html`. `Post#cook` returns that HTML unchanged, so scripts, event-handler attributes, and dangerous links in feed content survive into rendered forum posts. The feed polling path does not use the Readability allowlist used by remote article imports. Sanitize imported HTML before storing/rendering it, including on updates, rather than treating external feed content as trusted forum-origin HTML.

findings.title: Feed polling fails on entries without a content element
findings.body: The poller unconditionally calls `scrub` on `i.content`. Valid RSS feeds commonly supply their body in `description` or `content:encoded`, and Atom entries may supply only a summary; these entries need not have `content`. A missing value causes an exception and aborts the entire poll, including subsequent entries. Select the supported body fields with fallbacks and explicitly handle entries with no body. The current tests only check delegation and never parse a feed.

findings.title: URL rewriting corrupts protocol-relative links and misses relative paths
findings.body: The URL conversion treats every href beginning with `/` as a path on the article host. For example, `//cdn.example.com/image.jpg` becomes `http://article-host/cdn.example.com/image.jpg`; the image loop has the same problem. Conversely, document-relative references such as `images/photo.jpg` or `../other-post` remain unchanged and resolve against the forum instead of the source article. Resolve references against the complete source URL using URI joining so imported links and images continue to work.
